requirement: Home shows a Today card for the next meal slot, picked from local time and the family schedule, with one primary suggestion and two alternates.
assessment: Time-selected card and alternates exist; meal times are hard-coded instead of a configurable family schedule. Browser onboarding/Today covered; physical-device speed pending.

requirement: Swiping a card left shows the next candidate; swiping right accepts it. Accepting creates a planned meal and, if enabled, a Cook Card (M4).
assessment: Accept/Next and swipe implementation exist; an accepted Today plan offers a separate Send button rather than the specified enabled cook handoff. Manual paths bypass rules (D05). Native swipe validation pending.

requirement: Context chips above the card: Low energy, Quick (<20 min), Guests, Rainy/Cold (auto from weather), Sick-day light food, Sunday special, Use leftovers. Each chip re-ranks immediately.
assessment: Context chips and ingredient weights present; weather network failure/rain/cold exercised with mocks. Browser chip surfaces exercised. Mobile 300ms timing pending.

requirement: Ask box (text or voice): natural-language constraints such as "something with paneer, no onion, under 30 minutes". The LLM turns this into filters and weights; the ranker still makes the choice.
assessment: No natural-language ask box, constraint contract or ask-to-ranker integration.

requirement: Familiar ↔ Adventurous dial (0–100) sets how many never-cooked catalogue dishes can appear. Default 20.
assessment: Six preset dial buttons exist rather than a continuous slider; zero does not limit novel dishes (D15).

requirement: A "Why this?" tap shows the top three score drivers in plain language.
assessment: Why this shows score drivers; implementation displays up to four instead of the specified top three. Browser control exists; core reasons tested.

requirement: Home-screen widget (Android and iOS) shows the Today card with Accept and Next.
assessment: No Android/iOS home-screen widget implementation/configuration.

requirement: What's available: a strip of vegetable chips (seasonal, from the family's usual buys) plus recorded leftovers. Ticking what's in the kitchen boosts dishes that use them. Two further options always show: "Order a missing item" (Blinkit) and "Order in" (Zomato).
assessment: Vegetable/leftover strip and both commerce entry points exist. Vegetables come from recent history plus a fixed list, with no seasonality. Leftover chips toggle one global boost rather than selecting a specific leftover.

requirement: Family with members; each member has a role (Planner, Cook, Eater, Shopper), an age band (toddler, child, teen, adult, senior) and optional WhatsApp number. Age sets defaults: milder spice and smaller portions for young children, softer and lighter food for seniors.
assessment: Roles, age bands and optional phone fields exist. Child spice defaults are set at member creation; changing age does not recalculate them. Age-based portion sizes are missing (D09).

requirement: Hard rules per member: diet (veg, egg, non-veg, vegan, Jain, satvik), exclusions (onion-garlic, specific ingredients), allergies, spice tolerance.
assessment: Diet/Jain/onion flags and literal exclusions work in controls. Allergy families, complete ingredients, hard spice and custom-dish safety fail (D01–D05).

requirement: Day rules: recurring (no meat on Tuesdays), lunar calendar fasts (Ekadashi, Pradosh), festival windows (Navratri, Ramzan, Shravan), each tied to members. The system ships a preloaded panchang calendar that the family can edit.
assessment: Weekday no-meat/fast, Ekadashi and Navratri rules exist. Pradosh, Ramzan and Shravan absent. No UI edits bundled calendar dates, custom fast assignments or school holidays; 2027 dates explicitly approximate. D25.

requirement: One base, many plates: when rules conflict, suggest a base dish with per-member variants (for example sabudana khichdi for the fasting member, a regular version for others) and show who each plate is for.
assessment: Recommendations produce split plates; persisted meals reduce groups to a single member or no member (D09), with independent dishes rather than an explicit shared-base/variant model.

requirement: Onboarding takes under 2 minutes: family name, members, rules, and "pick 10 dishes you make often" from a regional catalogue, used as cold-start history.
assessment: Three-step onboarding works and was completed with ten favourites. Primary planner's rules can only be edited after finishing; skips allow no cold-start picks. Under-two-minute target not measured in an unassisted user trial.

requirement: Catalogue packs at launch: North Indian, South Indian and General (pan-India), with local dish names and aliases. More regions come later.
assessment: North/South/general catalogue and Latin aliases exist; existing catalogue uniqueness/link integrity tests pass. See vegan coverage and Indic custom-ID defects (D04/D21); no language-specific alias model.

requirement: Create family: any user can create a family and becomes its first Planner. Others join with a signed, expiring invite link (app or WhatsApp). A person can belong to more than one family (for example parents' home).
assessment: Multiple local families and switching exist. Shared identities, signed expiring invitations, invite acceptance and live cloud sync are absent; store/README explicitly defer them.

requirement: Free-text preferences in English, for the family or one member: "prefer healthier options", "less spicy for kids", "no maida on weekdays". The LLM turns each into a visible soft rule (a weight on tags such as fried, spice, millet) that the user can edit or delete. Preferences never override hard rules.
assessment: Visible soft weights and optional LLM parse exist. Negation is inverted (D19), no saved preference/weight editor, and no-maida is approximated as fried-food reduction rather than refined-flour matching.

requirement: Voice log using free on-device speech recognition (Android and iOS cover Hindi, English and major Indic languages), including code-mixed speech ("aaj dinner mein rajma chawal aur raita"): parsed into dishes, slot and date, confirmed with one tap.
assessment: English/Hinglish text parsing and keyboard dictation path exist. No hold-mic on-device recognition flow; Android RECORD_AUDIO explicitly blocked. Hindi-script parser fails (D20); Indic custom IDs collide (D21). Voice p90 pending.

requirement: Photo log: the image model suggests the dish names; the user confirms. The April photo flow stays but becomes optional.
assessment: Camera/gallery, optional Gemini recognition and confirm-before-save code exist. Camera permissions declared. Live camera/native capture and paid recognition not exercised; no API key supplied.

requirement: Auto-log: an accepted plan becomes a cooked meal after its slot ends unless the user changes it. A 9 pm digest lists anything unconfirmed.
assessment: Pure autoLog/idempotency/manual replacement controls pass. Application trigger misses active slot boundaries (D37), no 9pm digest (D33), and correction states fail (D07/D08).

requirement: Cook photos sent back over WhatsApp attach to the planned meal as proof and log it.
assessment: No WhatsApp incoming photo ingestion, attachment or cook-proof logging flow.

requirement: Quick-reuse chips show the last 8 distinct dishes for one-tap logging.
assessment: Last eight distinct dishes appear as reuse chips. A chip creates a draft requiring Save, rather than one-tap logging. Browser reuse shelf observed.

requirement: Cook Card: when the Planner confirms a day's meals, the app opens WhatsApp with the card pre-filled for the cook's chat (click-to-chat or share sheet, free). A reminder fires at a set time (default 9:30 pm the day before) if the card hasn't been sent.
assessment: Cook Card preview/click-to-chat and reminder function exist. Sent status means composer opened (D36); reminder cancellation/condition fails (D32), and global rescheduling removes other cards (D29). No actual message sent in testing.

requirement: The card is in the cook's language and script, with an optional voice note generated by the phone's free on-device text-to-speech and attached as audio.
assessment: Five-language headings and device read-aloud exist. No generated audio file attached to WhatsApp; dish names/quantities remain English (D42). Low-literacy full voice path absent.

requirement: Quantities scale to headcount (for example "rice 2 cups, dal 1 cup for 5 people") from catalogue portion metadata; per-member variants are called out.
assessment: Headcount quantities exist only for a subset of dishes. No adult-equivalent child portions; split headcounts are wrong (D09); alternate selection shows old quantities (D41).

requirement: The card carries a link to a no-login Cook page (signed link, free static hosting). The cook taps OK, Missing item or Change dish there. "Missing item" feeds the M6 list; "Change" shows the Planner two alternates.
assessment: Static no-login page and manually pasted WhatsApp replies exist. No signed expiry (D24), automatic backend update/shopper notification, validated reply ID (D23), or persistent Change/alternates workflow (D22). Reply phone normalization fails (D34).

requirement: The cook's repertoire: dishes the cook knows are tagged; suggestions favour them when the cook is scheduled.
assessment: Ranker reads cook.repertoire; no screen lets the planner/cook populate or edit it.

requirement: Cook schedule (days, slots, leave) sets which slots produce Cook Cards.
assessment: Cook day/slot controls exist, but Cook Card ignores working days and treats empty slots as unrestricted (D35). No dated leave management.

requirement: Prioritised choices: per slot the Planner can approve up to 3 ranked options (1st, 2nd, backup). The cook picks the highest one she can make with what's available and taps it on the Cook page. A "standing menu bank" of pre-approved dishes lets the cook choose on days the Planner doesn't plan.
assessment: Three ranked choices and Cook page selection work. No standing pre-approved menu bank for unplanned days; chosen alternate persistence/quantities fail (D06/D41).

requirement: Family vote: the planner shares 2–3 options to the family WhatsApp group as a vote link (free web page); it closes at a set time and the winner is planned.
assessment: No timed family vote page/link, vote closure or winner-to-plan workflow.

requirement: Kid mode: a picture-card swipe on the planner's phone ("Yum / Meh"), with no account needed.
assessment: No picture-card Yum/Meh kid mode.

requirement: Tiffin return check: a notification after school pick-up asks "How did the tiffin come back?" (Empty, Half, Full). This is a strong acceptance signal per child.
assessment: Empty/Half/Full controls and local reminder functions exist. Holiday/box/time behavior fails (D28/D30/D31); T scores leak between boxes (D17); no optional reason after repeated Full. Real native push/tap pending.

requirement: Quick reactions after a meal (Loved it, OK, Not again) per member; the April feedback chips map onto these.
assessment: Per-member Loved/OK/Not again controls work; browser child reaction and history persistence exercised; mutually exclusive reaction control passes.

requirement: After logging, "Anything left over?" records the leftover dish and a rough amount.
assessment: Manual lunch/dinner logs offer rough amounts and one selected leftover; browser save/prompt exercised. Auto-logs and other slots have no leftover capture prompt, and multi-dish leftovers require repeated flows.

requirement: Leftover chains: the catalogue holds transformations (dal to dal paratha, rice to lemon rice, sabzi to frankie). Leftovers boost linked dishes for the next 1–2 slots. What the family actually did with each leftover is recorded and learned (section 8).
assessment: Catalogue transformations boost ranking and prior decisions are read. Reuse is inferred from dish identity without confirmation (D11/D12); window is two days rather than the specified next one–two slots. D learning counts do not use the stated 60-day decay.

requirement: Staples, not inventory: the family ticks about 25 staples it keeps; the system assumes they are there unless marked out. No item-level stock tracking.
assessment: Default staple list and editable comma-separated values exist. Out-of-stock can be represented by removing an item; no item inventory was introduced.

requirement: Blinkit cart handoff: for planned meals, list ingredients not in staples, merge them with the cook's "Missing item" taps, and open Blinkit with a search per item (deep link), or share the list to Zepto, Instamart or WhatsApp. Moves to a cart API if a partnership becomes possible.
assessment: Cook/manual/plan lists merge with search/copy/WhatsApp handoff. Missing ingredients incomplete (D14), completed items suppress future needs (D13), plan confirmation does not auto-create cart entries, and UI covers only next three days. No Zepto/Instamart direct sharing.

requirement: A monthly "food saved" counter based on leftover chains used.
assessment: No monthly food-saved counter.

requirement: Order in with Zomato: when the family picks "Order in", the app suggests 3 dishes that fit the day's rules and recent pattern (for example "no North Indian for 3 days") and opens Zomato with a search. The order is logged as a meal so the history stays complete.
assessment: Three order-in cards, Zomato search and explicit Log as ordered in exist. Actual ordering/deep-link compatibility pending; dietary metadata issues apply and ordered meals incorrectly consume leftovers (D12).

requirement: Tomorrow plan push at a time the user sets (default 9 pm): tomorrow's breakfast, tiffins and lunch suggestions, confirmed in one tap.
assessment: Configured daily local reminder and one-tap Tomorrow confirmation exist. Push text is generic, not the computed meal/tiffin shortlist; multi-family scheduling fails (D29). Real native reminder/tap and 15s target pending.

requirement: 7-day family calendar: a week grid (days × slots, one row per tiffin per child) where meals can be pinned, dragged and swapped; unpinned slots fill with live suggestions. Rules, fasts, festivals, guests and school holidays show on the calendar. The week can be shared to WhatsApp as an image.
assessment: Seven-day list, pin/edit and long-press/tap swaps exist. No drag grid, occasion/guest/holiday display or image sharing; week is shared as text. Unsafe swap path (D05), selected alternate mismatch (D06). Live unpinned days compute independently and may repeat dishes across the week.

requirement: Occasion planner: event name, date, guest list (named guest groups), headcount and rules. It builds a menu of starter, main, bread or rice, sweet, and avoids dishes served to the same guest group before.
assessment: No occasions, named guest groups, guest rules/headcount, five-course menu, prior-hosting avoidance, preparation timeline or Served memory.

requirement: Life modes that change ranking for a date range: Exam week (light, familiar), Travel (pause), Guests staying, Recovery (light food), Festival.
assessment: No date-range Exam/Travel/Guests/Recovery/Festival life modes.

requirement: Festival packs (Diwali, Onam, Pongal, Eid, Christmas, Durga Puja) offered 7 days ahead, based on the family's region and calendar.
assessment: No festival menu packs offered seven days ahead; simple calendar festival labels are not this feature.

requirement: Two tiffins per child: each school-going child can have a short-break box (small, dry, finger food) and a lunch box. Both are suggested as a pair, kept distinct from each other and from breakfast, and planned the evening before. School days and holidays come from a per-child school calendar.
assessment: School days and two enabled boxes appear per child; initial distinct primaries and pure holiday filtering pass. No holiday editing UI; saved alternatives can repeat (D10), box fit incomplete (D27), member identity can be lost (D38), reminders ignore holidays (D30).

requirement: Each catalogue dish carries food-group tags: cereal, millet, pulse, vegetable, green leafy, dairy, egg or meat, fried.
assessment: Catalogue defines food-group tags and ranking uses them. Tag/ingredient completeness needs a food-domain audit; no nutritional target or calorie model was added.

requirement: Balance rings show the week against simple targets based on ICMR-NIN 2024 (for example pulses at least 5 days, green leafy at least 3, millets at least 2, fried at most 2). No calories.
assessment: No weekly balance rings or pulses/greens/millets/fried target view.

requirement: Ranking adds a small boost for a group that is behind ("No greens since Monday"). The household can switch this off.
assessment: Switchable greens/millet boosts exist. Pulse/fried weekly targets and weekly deficit model absent; based mainly on last-seen day and minimum entry count.

requirement: Timeline history grouped by date with thumbnails, member filters and search. This closes the April gaps.
assessment: Date-grouped history, thumbnails, member filters and search exist. Browser two-day logs/search/reaction and reload persistence covered; native thumbnail retention/delete pending.

requirement: Family favourites shelf built automatically from repeated positive outcomes, with a "safe choice" badge.
assessment: Automatic favourites shelf exists but safe-choice confidence can derive only from neutral frequency (D18).

requirement: Heirloom recipes: record a voice note (for example Nani explaining her sambar), stored with transcript and linked to the dish.
assessment: No heirloom audio recording, transcript storage or dish association.

requirement: Monthly and yearly "Year in food" recap (most-loved dish, new dishes tried, leftovers saved), shareable as an image.
assessment: No monthly/yearly food recap or shareable image.

requirement: Every suggestion has a reason string built from its top drivers.
assessment: Reason strings exist and are generated from drivers; baseline reason control passes. Reason correctness inherits metadata defects such as Fits everyone's rules for milk-allergic meals (D01).

requirement: Hide dish (forever or for 30 days); pause learning; reset recommendations.
assessment: Hide forever/30 days, pause and reset UI exist. Pause scope fails UI promise (D16); reset leaves history-based habits/recency intact. Hidden settings are local-device only.

requirement: Consent: each member's WhatsApp number is added only after they opt in via a link; the cook can opt out from the Cook page.
assessment: Planner can tick They agreed and Cook page sends STOP. No member-owned opt-in link, signed consent record or validated opt-out token; STOP still requires planner manual paste and reply card ID is ignored (D23).

requirement: Export the household's data (JSON or CSV) and delete it within 30 days, in line with India's DPDP Act.
assessment: JSON/CSV export code and immediate local record deletion exist. Browser JSON download capture timed out so downloaded-content verification is outstanding; photos remain after native deletion (D39). No server lifecycle/retention service because cloud storage is absent.
